precepts.why:
Ezekiel was set down “in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”, and they were “very dry.” A valley full of bones is a graveyard. Very dry means no nourishment, no understanding, no water. David names that same valley: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.”

That was a rap lyric, huh? Shame on you. That is in the Bible. It is not Coolio and it is not Tupac. The world took the words of the famous Christian prayer and made a song of them, but the valley of the shadow of death is a real place in the scripture.

It is the same darkness Job spoke about in Job 10:21 and 22. It is the same land Baruch spoke of earlier, where our people wax old and are defiled with the dead in a strange land. And it is the same place Isaiah speaks of when the Lord comes to bring out “them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” The valley of dry bones, the valley of the shadow of death, the land of darkness and the prison house are all one place: the lands of our captivity.

So the valley Ezekiel walked round about is where our people are today, dead and dry in a strange land. Yet even there the one who walks with the Lord fears no evil, because the Lord is with him, and it is the Lord who will bring those bones to life.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
The voice spake unto Peter the second time: “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” So what does God cleanse? Does he cleanse Esau? I never read that one. Ezekiel tells us who God cleanses.

“Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

Then: “but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” God says he is going to cleanse us, the twelve tribes.

So what God hath cleansed is Israel, the northern kingdom brought back to Judah. That is why Peter could go into Cornelius’ house. Christians read verses 34 and 35, “God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him”, and say God accepts everybody, that Cornelius was a white man, an Italian, a Roman. That is supersessionism, replacement theology. The next verse explains it: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel”.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them”. That is what Ezekiel 37 shows: “Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions”.

“And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.” That is the grafting: the stick of Joseph, Ephraim and the house of Israel, joined to the stick of Judah, and the two become one in God's hand.

So the wild olive tree is not the nations; it is the northern kingdom being joined back with Judah. That is why Paul warns, “Boast not against the branches.” Zechariah 12:7 says the same: that they do not magnify themselves against Judah. That magnify is telling you: do not be highminded, do not boast.

“Be not highminded, but fear”. The root that bears the graffed-in branch is Christ, and he is the one that holds the two sticks together as one.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
Revelation 7 names the tribe of Joseph but not Ephraim. How do we know Joseph there is Ephraim? Write the precept down: “Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim”. See that? Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim. That is how you know Joseph stands for Ephraim.

And God does not leave that stick by itself: “and the tribes of Israel his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand.”

Ephraim and the tribes of Israel his fellows are the northern kingdom; the stick of Judah is the southern kingdom. God puts them together and makes them one stick in his hand.

That is the same work James spoke of in Acts 15 and Amos prophesied, the tabernacle of David built again, and it is why Cornelius, a man of the northern kingdom, was received. Joseph and Judah are made one.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
When the voice told Peter, “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common”, Peter would have had to go to the Old Testament to explain what God had cleansed. He would go to Ezekiel 37: “I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” And whom was he gathering, and from where? “Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen”: they were living among the Gentiles, the nations. He gathers them, cleanses them, and takes the two kingdoms, the stick of Judah and the stick of Joseph in the hand of Ephraim, and makes them one.

Hosea shows the same joining: “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.” That is the two sticks becoming one in the Lord's hand.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The northern kingdom, cast out among the heathen and called not my people, would be called the sons of the living God again. That was the prophecy, and that is why Peter could not call those men common: the time had come, Peter, we have to gather them together, bring them together.

And guess what: that is happening now. It has been going on since back then until now. We are out in South America gathering God's people, out in Africa gathering God's people, and here in the States bringing God's people back together, Judah and Israel under one head.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
Peter says, “Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation”. That phrase “another nation” might throw you off, because Christians use it to say Peter was going to other races. Ezekiel shows what that other nation is: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

The kingdom of Judah was called a nation, and the kingdom of Israel, Ephraim and the rest, was called a nation. Two nations, two separate kingdoms, but one people. So when Peter the Jew, of Judah, speaks of coming unto one of another nation, that other nation is the kingdom of Israel, the northern kingdom. That is what the vision of the sheet was about: “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean”, speaking of Cornelius and his family.

Then Peter says God “is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” A Christian will stop you right there, but read the next verse: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ”. That tells you who Cornelius and his kinfolk were: the children of Israel, scattered in every nation.

Acts 15 looks back on this and quotes the prophets: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”. The regathering of the twelve tribes, the two kingdoms coming back together, is what Acts 10 is about. God is bringing the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom back into one nation, just as Ezekiel said.

precepts.why:
The Lord tells Edom, “I will even do according to thine anger, and according to thine envy which thou hast used out of thy hatred against them; and I will make myself known among them, when I have judged thee.” He will make himself known among us. How? Ezekiel shows it: “So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.”

The breath came into us. This is now. As war goes on, Edom is distracted by the nonsense with Iran, and meanwhile we are rising up. The word of God is spreading, and we are waking up as an exceeding great army.

That is God making himself known among his people while he judges Edom for the envy and hatred he used against us, for saying “These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it; whereas the Lord was there”. The Lord was there, and he is making himself known among us again.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Hosea says, “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”. The children of Judah are the nation; the children of Israel, the northern kingdom, are the company of nations. Gathered together means they become one, and the one head is Christ. You read the same thing from multiple prophets, and Ezekiel says it this way: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all”. The one king is the one head.

“and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”: no more southern and northern. Remember, one of them was not a nation at all. Isaiah said, “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.” Ephraim became Lo-ammi, not my people, Gentiles, heathen, uncircumcised, all the same. “Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things”. They are brought back together, just as Hosea said.

Christ said the same out of his own mouth: “I lay down my life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold”. This fold is Judah, because Christ is of Judah; the other sheep are the northern kingdom. “them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice”: they hear through the teachings of Judah first. “and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.” The one shepherd is Christ himself. He is quoting Hosea 1:10-11 and Ezekiel 37:22.

Even Caiaphas, who hated the Messiah, prophesied it: “that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” Those scattered abroad are the strangers of 1 Peter 1, the northern kingdom. The builders were appointed to reject Christ so he would be killed, and by his death the northern kingdom would get the chance to repent and be redeemed back into the fold. That could not be done unless Christ died.

So the not my people of Hosea 1 are the strangers Peter wrote to, “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God”. Christ gathers both kingdoms together as one nation under one king.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Peter said, “Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation”. Sound familiar? It is the same thing the woman at the well said to Christ: the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans. “but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean”. Any man, not food, not animals. The vision was about a man, Cornelius.

Who is one of another nation? In Genesis 35 Jacob was told a nation and a company of nations would come of him. Ezekiel shows the two becoming one: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”. Judah and Ephraim, both the houses, gathered together under one king.

“Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things, nor with any of their transgressions: but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” He will cleanse both kingdoms and make them clean.

So Cornelius was of another nation, another kingdom: the northern kingdom. Judah called the northern kingdom common and unclean, not my people, strangers. But what God hath cleansed, that call not thou common. God promised to cleanse them and make the two one nation, and that is why Peter could go into Cornelius's house.

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Paul says they were “having no hope, and without God in the world.” Who was without hope? Ezekiel shows it: “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts.”

They said it themselves: no hope. So Israel was the one without hope. “we are cut off for our parts”: we were alienated from the commonwealth. The dry bones are the whole house of Israel, not another nation.

So every part of Ephesians 2:12 lines up with Israel. The ones cut off, the ones with their hope lost, the aliens from the commonwealth, were the house of Israel itself, and that is who the letter is speaking to.

precepts.why:
“For he is our peace, who hath made both one.” He is the peace of the saints Paul writes to in Ephesians 1:1. You have to know history to understand this verse, because why does it say both? Is it only talking about Jews and Gentiles? What happened in the history?

Ezekiel shows it: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” One king: Christ. No more two nations.

That is the both that he made one: the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. Jew and Gentile, circumcision and uncircumcision, are those same two kingdoms. When those two kingdoms were against each other they were at odds, and that hatred was the middle wall of partition.
